title: For people using Godot, how are you creating UI?
author: Crignog
selftext: I have used SpriteCook to generate some ui and it looks fine, but not great. Any tips on creating UI that looks good?

comments.author: AlgaeNo3373
comments.body:
Iterating bit by bit tbh. I did some html mockups first to figure out what I actually wanted, more or less, then used that as reference for Godot integration. Here's 3 steps of iteration going from placeholder text to mockup UI to iterated version of it. 

https://preview.redd.it/lskcsyaz9voh1.png?width=818&format=png&auto=webp&s=bf03c759dbd675f816bdbf7ff65eab44a0f487cb

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: That looks great! Appreciate that. But yes I should have been more specific. I meant how are people using tools to actually create the art for the UI

replies.author: AlgaeNo3373
replies.body:
Cheers :) to be clear in this instance, no tools used. I just asked for progressively more specific things in natural language terms. I don't particularly love the term but I suppose it applies here: the LLM itself is the tool, in many cases. 

Sometimes, for layout/organization/mockups I'll use Miro (or you could swap it for any kind of flow-chart diagramming interface).  
  
 [https://mesocosms.net/devlogs/how-to-draw-a-thread/](https://mesocosms.net/devlogs/how-to-draw-a-thread/) \- this devlog shows how I used a miro screenshot to guide some UI work by Claude Code. Didn't help much, tbh. Astra is more useful for UI iteration atm. 

Unless by "art for UI" you mean something else? \^\^

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Hey thanks for the detailed response! I have provided the artwork to be used in creating the UI in my game, but that art was generated using SpriteCook and is just a bit blurry/stretches poorly is all. Sorry I don't know if that really helps answer the question haha

replies.author: AlgaeNo3373
replies.body: For sure :) I've had some success lately using UI mockups as inspo to feed into Astra for UI fuckery, if that's worth anything. Could well work with other models too. I asked for  "animated UI elements" in an opening scene, dropped a whole array of stock "sci fi" UI elements, and got back a bunch of integrated animated elements that I then tweaked a bit. So it's defs possible to take your UI elements in-game, might just need to use it as inspo rather than directly port the raw images if they're blurring, etc.

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Okay awesome, thank you for your help!

comments.author: Onye_Nacho
comments.body: Is your question asking us how we make UI in general (even manually) or how we use GAI tools to create UI?

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Apologies, I meant using GAI tools to create the elements to use in UI

replies.author: Onye_Nacho
replies.body:
I see...

Well in my case, I don't ever bother using GAI for user interfaces. I think they are useless for that. I'd rather just make them manually. I seldom even use it for artwork since they are still too unreliable for my own creative needs. I mainly bother with GAI tools when it comes to music, sound effects, and especially voice acting.

comments.author: KuraudoRyo
comments.body: Using Claude Design with Godot Instructions worked pretty well for me

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: I didn't even realise Claude Design was a thing! I'll definitely take a look

comments.author: NewKindaSpecial
comments.body: codex generates the art and builds a local webserver with options to choose from. I pick the UI design I like and it integrates it. Not sure I would want to use godot for 3d but with 2d its pretty damn good. Having a headless engine has been more seamless than unreals MCP I've found. Though maybe I just suck with it.

replies.body: That does look great! does it scale nicely?

replies.author: Livid_Shallot5701
replies.body: It's actually super huge because I singled out each individual part so every thing had the whole screen for itself

comments.author: Ok_Island5421
comments.body: I create my design as vectors in Affinity. Then I export each individual part as an SVG, along with one complete SVG of the assembled design. I use the complete SVG as a blueprint and have the AI recreate it in Godot using the individual parts. This way, each part can actually work as intended. Buttons, sliders, health bar, and other dynamic elements with animations or shaders. I give it a font so the AI can add labels that match the original designs dynamic text like for example a ammo counter or dialogue text.

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: I will look into this, thanks!

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: Created some basic concept art of what i wanted the UI to be like -> Threw it into GPT and iterated on it until I was happy with the details and feel -> Used the concept art as ref to create SVGs of the elements in Inkscape (more optimized, infinitely scalable, etc.)

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Sorry, did you create them in Inkscape yourself just using the revised AI images as references?
